transcript.text: I confirmed with our company's insurance broker yesterday that our cyber policy covers this AI platform deployment only if the vendor maintains at least $5,000,000 of cyber-liability insurance and names the company as an additional insured. I received the broker's written confirmation yesterday, but I have not yet added this requirement to the approval checklist. This means the vendor's draft insurance provisions need to be revised to include these two conditions — the $5,000,000 cyber-liability insurance minimum and naming our company as an additional insured — before Elena can sign this agreement. Without these, our cyber policy would not cover this deployment, which creates a significant exposure gap.

transcript.text: I've reviewed the enterprise customer's existing master agreement and confirmed that the company may use an AI subcontractor for support only if the subcontractor grants an annual audit right and accepts uncapped indemnity for both confidentiality breaches and personal-data breaches. I have not yet incorporated those flow-down requirements into the vendor agreement. These two conditions — the annual audit right and the uncapped indemnity for confidentiality and personal-data breaches — need to be added to the vendor agreement before Elena signs, because our enterprise customer contract requires them as a condition of using an AI subcontractor for support functions.
